title: Launch Automation Builds (launch-c v1)
description: Emitted by launch-c/plan_reader.py from the U-CONTRACT launch plan plus the Skill 50 P4 DRAFT-ONLY build plans. One entry per launch-plan automation unit, carrying the launch-plan fields unchanged and the Skill 50 workflows it waits on. DRAFT-ONLY: nothing here authorizes a send, a publish or a live switch-on.

owner_acknowledgement.description: Late start: promotional sends already in the past are DROPPED (their builds stay ready for the still-future steps). The owner acknowledges that exact list by passing dropped_sends_hash back (--acknowledge-dropped-sends).

calendar.description: L07 compiled launch calendar: normalized ISO instants, IANA zone and DST overlap flag. Phase order is the shared calendar law's (validated by the shared launch-plan validator), including the Black Friday teaser, countdown, cyber_monday and last_call instants.

schedule_policy.description: Deterministic evaluation instant and suppression policy for this compile.

journal.description: Stable unit keys mapped to the expected graph hash the builder journals and verifies on readback.

unused_build_plan_workflows.description: Build plans that could not be bound to a launch email_sequence. Reported, never silently dropped; pass --sequence-map to bind one.

text_builds.description: One entry per launch text_set: the build unit the texts are delivered as (template launch-text-set). blocked_by names 'text_set:<id> copy' when working/text/<id>.sms.json is absent or invalid. Present only when the plan carries text sets.

variant_tag.description: The contact tag the short post-sale handler sets for the purchased variant (main / upsell-N / downsell-N), carried verbatim from the launch plan's automation unit. The launch compiler binds it to the buildable template's variant placeholder, which is what lets the short handler install its template graph instead of falling back to its email sequence. Null when the plan declares none.

followed_offer_id.description: The offer an upsell/downsell follow-up follows, carried verbatim from the launch plan's automation unit. The launch compiler gates the follow-up's sends on the tag purchased-<this id> (not the launch-wide buyer tag, which the main-offer buyer already carries). Null when the plan declares none; a follow-up build is then blocked.

settings.description: The launch plan's automations[].settings block, carried verbatim (reentry allow|block, enrollment single|successive). Null when the plan declares none; the compiler then records the setting insufficient instead of guessing.

allow_reentry.description: The native reentry boolean derived from settings.reentry: true for allow, false for block, null when the plan declares none. True/false is APPLIED to the workflow settings and read back after the save; null applies nothing.

allow_enrollment.description: settings.enrollment as declared, or null when the plan declares none. Applied natively as the top-level workflow boolean allowMultiple (single=false, successive=true — captured live, see evidence/F05-capability.json) and proven per build by the post-save readback, never by the request.

enrollment.description: Enrolment mode, carried from the launch plan's automation settings.enrollment. successive keeps a SECOND purchase's fulfilment, deduplicated by the native event/transaction/line identity, and is refused when the same unit declares reentry blocked. Read by the installable compiler's purchase_identity.

purchase_identity.description: The purchase-event identity the post-sale handler deduplicates on, carried verbatim from the launch plan (native field references only). Null when the plan declares none: the compiler records purchase_identity.sufficient false rather than normalising an order id into a key.

email_sequences.description: Launch email_sequence ids this automation waits on, in plan order.

workflows.description: Skill 50 DRAFT workflows bound to those sequences, steps passed through verbatim.

state.description: blocked when any email_sequence this automation waits on has no bound Skill 50 build plan, or nothing is left to build. A blocked build is never upgraded by assumption; the reader exits 4 when any build is blocked.

blocked_by.description: Why the build is blocked. A bare id is a missing email_sequence build plan, except the three words lifecycle, eligibility and sender, which mean the bound Skill 50 build plan carried none of that metadata (the reader never supplies its own); prefixed reasons name page_url:, email_count:, text_set:, upstream:, guards: or schedule_suppressed: (send that cannot land before doors close) failures; no_future_sends and no_buildable_workflow mean nothing is left to build. Past sends never block: they are dropped (see dropped_sends). A blocked build is never upgraded by assumption.

eligibility.description: Enrollment/eligibility rules carried verbatim from the Skill 50 build plan; named references only.

lifecycle.description: Stop and suppression rules compiled into provider-native conditions/settings. Purchase suppresses this campaign only; entitled access is never suppressed.

lifecycle_source.description: Where the lifecycle came from: build_plan when the bound Skill 50 build plan carried it, null when it carried none (the build is then blocked by lifecycle). The reader never supplies a lifecycle of its own.

sender.description: Sender configuration REFERENCES only (never credential values).

content_hashes.description: Declared Skill 50 content hashes per workflow key.

text_sets.description: Launch text_set ids this automation waits on (the texts the client elected for it), in plan order. Present only when the automation waits on at least one text set.

bindings.description: Approved copy the reader bound into this build. sms_copy maps an SMS step id (or its body_ref) to the Skill 50 approved body from working/text/<set_id>.sms.json; the compiler binds it and the build command refuses an elected SMS step that stays copy_pending. Present only when the automation waits on a text set.

suppressed.description: Schedule nodes suppressed by past-time policy or close-time suppression. A builder skips every step listed here.

dropped_sends.description: The PAST-TIME-SUPPRESSED subset of suppressed: sends dropped because they were already in the past when the launch was compiled (late start), pending owner acknowledgement.
